Devin: Quick update — I ran a full nsys capture on ded-gpu-3 to repro the latency spike. Full instrumented trace increased observed tail latency by ~45% and reported ~2.2x GPU time due to synchronous post-processing. Attaching a short timeline snapshot below.

Maria: Oof. Where are the hotspots (kernel names)?

Devin: Main hotspots: aten::layer_norm (fwd), custom_attention_kv_merge, and two small memcpy kernels that line up with KV cache flushes. Timeline shows a lot of tiny kernels (~200us) causing high kernel-launch overhead.

Ash: This is why full traces are risky in prod. Sampling avoids most overhead but misses short-lived kernels. We need production guardrails: default sampling (1Hz) + automatic full trace only on anomaly.

Devin: I tried 1Hz sampling with nsys; it captured layer_norm regressions but missed the small memcpy spikes tied to cache evictions. So sampling alone can't show KV behavior.

Janet: Could we do hybrid: keep low-rate sampling + lightweight NVTX around KV code paths so sampled traces can correlate with KV events without full instrumentation?

Ash: NVTX + counters are cheap. Push NVTX ranges around kv insert/evict and emit a small counter. Then sampled traces get context.

Kai: Also adjust batching heuristics: coalesce small sequences. In sims, increasing batch max_items from 32 -> 48 reduced number of memcpys by ~40% and removed many tiny kernels.

Devin: Proposed guardrail plan: 1) default 1Hz sampling in prod; 2) enable NVTX for KV code paths; 3) on anomaly (latency > p95 * 1.5) auto-trigger a 30s full nsys capture with retention/ACL.

perf-bot: Note: full nsys captures increase disk & bandwidth. Limit: 3 full captures per host per day. Policy perf/captures/retention=30d.

Maria: We should document overhead: approx numbers for sampling, NVTX, and full trace. Devin can you paste measured numbers?

Devin: Measured on ded (A100), seq_len=1024: sampling @1Hz -> median +3%, p99 +8%. NVTX only -> median +0.6%, p99 +1.2%. Full instrumented nsys -> median +28%, p99 +52%.

Liam: For kernel selection: current heuristic picks fused_attention if seq_len < 512 else block_attention. That logic misfires on mixed batches and causes kernel churn. Suggest picking kernel per microbatch rather than per-request-batch.

Ash: Agree. Kernel churn causes repeated kernel module loads and many tiny launches. Microbatch-level kernel pinning + reuse reduces launch overhead.

Maria: Action items: Devin add NVTX PR; Ash implement microbatch kernel pinning; Kai tune batching heuristic & re-run sims; Janet add instrumentation + anomaly-triggered capture workflow in ops.

Devin: I'll add a small helper commands snippet for ops: 

```
# lightweight sampling
nsys profile --sample=1000 --trace=nvtx,cuda --output=out_sample
# full (triggered on anomaly, short duration)
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=record --output=out_full --duration=30
```

Janet: For safety, captures must redact env and have restricted access. Use perf-bot to stash captures to S3 with encryption and ACL.

perf-bot: Policy applied: captures -> s3://redwood-perf/captures/prod/<host>/<ts> (access=restricted).

Kai: When enabling NVTX, avoid spamming every cache op. Use coalesced NVTX batches: group ops within a 5ms window into a single NVTX range.

Ash: :thumbsup: I'll own kernel pinning PR. Devin, assign me the trace that shows kernel load churn.

Devin: Done — assigned and attaching a tiny timeline snippet here: 

TIMELINE (ms): [0.00-0.15] memcpy HtoD 0.15ms; [0.40-4.20] aten::layer_norm 3.8ms; [4.50-10.70] custom_attention 6.2ms; [11.0-11.2] memcpy DtoH 0.2ms; repeated short kernels every 15-40ms.

Maria: Nice. Let's sync tomorrow at 13:00 PST to finalize thresholds and runbook.
